\section[scattare]{scattare — to take (a photo); to spring}

\label{lesson:IT-C506-scattare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for model making, then the Italian for to assemble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: scattare}
\textbf{scattare} — \textquotedblleft{}to take (a photo); to spring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho scattato cento foto in vacanza.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I took a hundred photos on holiday.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Scattare una foto} — to take a photo; \emph{lo scatto} is one shot.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{scattare} is not settled; it may be built on an old verb \emph{cattare} \textquotedblleft{}to catch\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scattare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scattare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{scattare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for model making, then the Italian for to assemble, then say \emph{scattare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does scattare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To take (a photo); to spring\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[inquadrare]{inquadrare — to frame (a shot)}

\label{lesson:IT-C506-inquadrare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to assemble, then the Italian for to take.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inquadrare}
\textbf{inquadrare} — \textquotedblleft{}to frame (a shot)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Inquadra bene il paesaggio prima di fare la foto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Frame the landscape well before you take the photo.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{quadro} \textquotedblleft{}square, picture\textquotedblright{}; also to put in context.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inquadrare} is built on \emph{quadro} \textquotedblleft{}a square, a picture\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{quadrum} \textquotedblleft{}a square\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inquadrare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inquadrare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{inquadrare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to assemble, then the Italian for to take, then say \emph{inquadrare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[il treppiede]{il treppiede — tripod}

\label{lesson:IT-C506-treppiede}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to take, then the Italian for to frame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il treppiede}
\textbf{il treppiede} — \textquotedblleft{}tripod\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Per le foto di notte serve il treppiede.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For night photos you need a tripod.}
\end{quote}

Also spelt \emph{treppiedi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{treppiede} is built from \emph{tre} \textquotedblleft{}three\textquotedblright{} and \emph{piede} \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{pēs, pedis} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il rullino]{il rullino — roll of film}

\label{lesson:IT-C506-rullino}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to frame, then the Italian for tripod.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il rullino}
\textbf{il rullino} — \textquotedblleft{}roll of film\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho trovato un vecchio rullino nel cassetto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I found an old roll of film in the drawer.}
\end{quote}

From the days before digital photos.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rullino} is a little form of \emph{rullo} \textquotedblleft{}roller\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Latin \emph{rotulus} \textquotedblleft{}a little wheel\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{rota} \textquotedblleft{}wheel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to frame, then the Italian for tripod, then say \emph{il rullino} again

\section[sviluppare]{sviluppare — to develop}

\label{lesson:IT-C506-sviluppare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for tripod, then the Italian for roll of film.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sviluppare}
\textbf{sviluppare} — \textquotedblleft{}to develop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho fatto sviluppare le foto in un negozio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I had the photos developed in a shop.}
\end{quote}

Also for ideas and skills: \emph{sviluppare un progetto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sviluppare} is built from \emph{s-} \textquotedblleft{}un-\textquotedblright{} and \emph{viluppo} \textquotedblleft{}a tangle\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists \emph{sviluppo}): to untangle, to unroll. The origin of \emph{viluppo} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sviluppare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for tripod, then the Italian for roll of film, then say \emph{sviluppare} again
\end{itemize}
